note: H3 proposes this contract and changes nothing. H4 implements it.

config.holds: user-authored settings: the service config file, the profile registry, generated profile configs, sync key material

data.holds: the library itself: the SQLite database, the asset store, publication profiles

state.holds: things Notrios must remember across runs but the user did not write: sync carrier spools, sync backups, the catch-up inbox, the remote-media quarantine

cache.holds: anything reproducible from the library: projections, the Recoll index, the generated Recoll configuration

runtime.holds: work in flight that must not survive a reboot: backup staging, restore review, per-process temporary asset roots

linux.no_default_behavior: XDG names no fallback for a missing XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, and inventing one in /tmp would put staged plaintext backups in a world-traversable directory. Notrios falls back to <state>/runtime, created 0700, and reports that it did.

macos.note: macOS TMPDIR is already per-user and per-session.

program_assets.holds: immutable files shipped with the build: the web interface, migrations, seed help content, desktop metadata

external.holds: paths Notrios writes that are not under any Notrios root: the notrios:// URL handler desktop entry in the XDG applications directory, and any path a user's profile points at outside the standard roots

windows.default: the registry, via the URL protocol handler key

macos.default: the Launch Services database, via the app bundle's CFBundleURLTypes

external.note: Not a Notrios root. It is written into territory shared with other applications, so uninstall removes only the exact file it installed and purge never deletes a user profile path that lives here.

xdg_rules.absolute_required: A relative value in any XDG_* variable is invalid. The variable is ignored and the specified default is used, and the substitution is reported once at startup. It is never resolved against the working directory.
xdg_rules.empty_is_unset: An empty or whitespace-only value is treated as unset, per the specification.
xdg_rules.linux_only: XDG variables are honoured on Linux and other Unix systems that are not macOS. On macOS and Windows the native locations are authoritative and XDG_* is ignored, because a user who exports XDG_CONFIG_HOME for another tool has not asked Notrios to leave ~/Library.
xdg_rules.runtime_dir_ownership: XDG_RUNTIME_DIR must be owner-only and owned by the user. If it exists but fails that check, Notrios refuses it and falls back to <state>/runtime rather than staging plaintext there.

order: explicit: a path given on the command line or in an explicitly named config file
portable: a marker file named notrios-portable.txt beside the executable, whose presence selects a layout rooted at the executable's directory
installed: the native per-OS roots above
source: a checkout, detected by go.mod plus the module path beside the executable or working directory
mode_precedence.never: Portable mode is never inferred from the current directory, from the directory being writable, or from the absence of installed roots. Guessing portability from writability is how a USB stick and a home directory become the same decision.
source_mode_only: reading config/config.example.yaml relative to the working directory
resolving web/dist relative to the working directory

install_variables.prefix: /usr/local for a system install; $HOME/.local is the recommended default for make install
install_variables.DESTDIR: Staging prefix for packaging. It is prepended to installed artifact paths only. It is never prepended to a user's config, data, state, cache, or runtime roots, and package staging creates none of them.
install_variables.rationale: An unprivileged user-local install is the dogfooding case, needs no sudo, and matches where the desktop entry already goes.

manifest.note: Written by install, read by uninstall. Uninstall removes only paths listed here, under a validated install root, whose recorded hash still matches. A modified or foreign-owned artifact is preserved and reported.

embedded_not_installed.note: Read from the binary via //go:embed, so they are deliberately absent from installed_artifacts. Installing them would ship files nothing reads and invite a stale copy to diverge from the compiled one.

entries.note: Embedded, then written into the generated Recoll config directory at runtime, which is why it is cache rather than an installed artifact.

no_path_consumer.logs: Notrios writes no log file. Every diagnostic goes to stderr through the standard library logger, so the process's supervisor decides where it lands -- journald under a systemd unit, the terminal otherwise. The plan lists logs in scope; the audit's answer is that there is nothing to place, and adding a log root would be inventing a consumer rather than relocating one.
no_path_consumer.snapshot_images: The snapshot output root is fully caller-supplied with no default, and is recorded as an external consumer rather than a root.
